sections.title: The letter á
paragraphs: The letter (á) /a/ makes the sound /a/, heard in (água) /ˈa.ɡwɐ/, which means water. This letter can make three different sounds.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: For the first sound, relax your mouth and raise the middle of your tongue slightly. For the second sound, drop your jaw wide and keep your tongue low and flat. For the third sound, keep the same mouth shape, but send the air through your nose. Place your finger beneath your nostrils to feel the warm airflow.

sections.title: Spelling positions
paragraphs: In unstressed syllables or before nasal consonants, you pronounce the sound /ɐ/, as in (cama) /ˈkɐ.mɐ/. In stressed open syllables, you say the sound /a/, as in (pá) /pa/. When marked by a tilde or followed by a syllable-final nasal consonant, you produce the sound /ɐ̃/, as in (canto) /ˈkɐ̃.tu/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not pronounce the sound /ɐ/ like the vowel in cat. Keep your mouth less open, closer to the vowel in cup. Do not pronounce the nasal variant like an English vowel followed by an audible n sound. Keep your tongue from touching your upper gums, and send the air through your nose.
